Part History already records what happened to a part and who did it.

Counts, bin transfers, price and field edits, receipts from a purchase order. Every event is written as one pipe-delimited line in the Event column, with the staff member, the date and the time beside it.
There is no entry for retiring a part, because retiring a part is not possible. The nearest thing a shop can do is delete it, and a deleted part takes its history with it.
BEFORE · WHAT IS ON STAGING TODAY
Everything the shop has ever created is offered.
Nothing on a row says the part is dead.
New Part Request, on a work order
Catalog Part is required, and it is the first thing on the screen.

An inventory part cannot exist unless a matching catalog part already does, so adding one part off the shelf means creating two records in two places, in the right order. It is drawn in the required blue, which is the only field on the dialog that is.
A part cannot be retired from here, and nothing on the screen suggests retiring is possible at all.
Min and Max sit loose between Core Charge and Tags,
with nothing saying what they belong to or when they matter. Every part has them, because every part is tracked.
The destructive action available here is
, which removes the part outright. There is no middle option between keeping a part in everyone's way and deleting it.
The dialog a shop opens today when it clicks a row on the Inventory list.
A second place a part can be created.

button makes a catalog record, which is not the thing a shop sells; to sell it they then go to Inventory and create again. Two entry points that make two different kinds of record is how one physical part ends up as two entries with the same number.

Today a part starts from a Catalog Part pick, the first field on the screen. An inventory part cannot exist unless a matching catalog entry already does.

Description first, then Part Number. Both are free text (S7-R1). No Part Library selector and no lookup step (S7-R2). Inventory Tracking sits below the cost, Sell Price and Core Charge fields and above Tags, with the switch on by default (S4-R1, S4-R2). Min and Max sit under the switch (S4-R4).

Every empty required field shows its own error at the same time: "Description is a required field" and "Part number is a required field" (S7-N1, S7-N2). Category and Cost are required, as they are today.

Exactly one Part Library entry has the number typed, so the new part links to it (S7-R4, S7-R5). The entry keeps its own description (S7-R6). The descriptions differ, so the toast reads: "Part created. Linked to F40010212 in the Part Library. Its description "Slack Adjuster" was kept." (S7-R9). There is no toast when they match, or when a new entry is created (S7-R10).

With the switch off, Min and Max are hidden (S4-R5). The bin location section stays visible and is optional, so a bin can be set as a shelf reference (S4-R6). Creating a part with tracking off needs the 'Part Library & Inventory → Delete' permission (S8-R7). Editing other fields of a part that is already untracked needs the same access as editing a tracked part (S8-N1a).

CREATE A PART A parts manager adds a part by typing its description and part number. No Part Library pick, no lookup step. Read left to right. Board 1.0 is today's part dialog, traced from staging. Boards 1.1 to 1.6 are screenshots of the build, on Staging Heavy Duty data.
Part History records counts, transfers and field edits today. It does not say which location a change came from.
Edit Inventory Part for FF5507, "Fuel FIlter, Mack/Volvo". The Active badge sits in the title row (Story 13).

Description becomes "Fuel Filter, Mack/Volvo" and Part Number becomes FF5507A. Lethbridge stocks the same Part Library entry, so each field says so under it: "This also changes the description at 1 other location." (S13-R12) and "This also changes the part number at 1 other location." (S13-R16). Each message shows only while the value differs from the saved one (S13-R17).
The same part is renamed in place. It keeps its stock, its bins and its history.

A "Description updated" entry and a "Part number updated" entry, each with the original and the new value. Entries at the location where the change was made carry no "Changed at" (S10-R25 covers the other locations).
At Lethbridge the same part now reads FF5507A, "Fuel Filter, Mack/Volvo". Only the Create & Edit permission is needed, even though the change reaches another location (S8-R11).

The entries are written at Lethbridge too. They end with "| Changed at: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919", naming the location where the change was made (S10-R25). Staff, Date and Time keep their production widths; a long Event wraps onto a second line. This board's table is redrawn over the build screenshot. The build still narrows Staff, Date and Time when the Event lines are long; that needs fixing to match.

CORRECT A PART'S NUMBER OR DESCRIPTION FF5507 is stocked at Heavy Duty and at Lethbridge, with a typo in its description ("FIlter"). At Heavy Duty the user fixes the description and changes the number. Read left to right: the edit, the warnings, the list, then Part History here and at the other location. Board 2.0 is today's Part History, traced from staging.

Read left to right: the edit, the warnings, the list, then Part History here and at the other location. Board 2.0 is today
Today the only way to take a part out of daily work is Delete.
Part Status, Active or Inactive, sits under Part Number. The badge in the title row shows the saved status (Story 13).
Picking a status applies nothing yet. The badge keeps showing the saved status until the change is confirmed.

Save raises "Deactivate part?" (S10-R1, S10-R3). It opens with the part number and description (S10-R4), then the three lines of S10-R6, then the optional note (S10-R10). The note here reads "Superseded by N6801-06-04X". The red Deactivate button has Cancel to its left (S10-R11). The bulk confirmation (board 4.4) is the same dialog, built from the design system Modal and Button.
Every change in the dialog is saved, the status is applied, and the dialog closes with "Part deactivated." (S13-R22). The part leaves the Active tab.
The badge reads Inactive and Part Status is on Inactive (S9-R14).
Active picked, then Save: "Activate part?", the part, then "This part can be added to new work again." and nothing more (S10-R7). The Activate button is blue (S10-R11).
Typing "superseded" in the Part History search returns the Deactivated entries whose note contains it (S10-R27). The search reads the Event text as shown and the Staff name, for every kind of entry.
RETIRE ONE PART One part is set inactive from its own dialog, then brought back the same way. Read left to right. Board 3.0 is today's part dialog, traced from staging. It has no status control.

No Active and Inactive tabs, no checkboxes, and no way to change many parts at once. Screenshot of production code (main at 5b730a00660; the Inventory list is unchanged through v26.40.13), on Staging Heavy Duty data. The quantity column reads "Total Qty".
"Deactivate parts" sits between Cycle count and Export while the Active tab shows (S2-R1, S2-R2). A user without the Delete permission does not see it (S8-R3).

A checkbox column appears at the left (S2-R4). The bulk bar spans the list under the tabs, and the search and filter row moves under it (S2-R7). The bar shows the count, "selected" and the Deactivate button, disabled until a row is ticked (S2-R7b, S2-R8).
A click anywhere on a row ticks it instead of opening the part (S2-R5). The count reads 2.
"Deactivate parts?", "2 parts selected.", then the three lines of S10-R5 and the optional note. The Deactivate button is red (S10-R11).
1.4 Saved and linked to the Part Library entry
"2 parts updated." (S10-R12). The parts leave the Active tab without a page reload, the mode ends and the selection clears (S2-R12, S2-R14).
On the Inactive tab the menu entry reads "Activate parts" and turns on the same mode (S3-R1). The bar button reads Activate (S3-R2). The header checkbox ticks every loaded row (S2-R6).

"Activate parts?", "2 parts selected.", "These parts can be added to new work again." and "Existing records that use them stay as they are." (S10-R8). The Activate button is blue. On confirm the parts leave the Inactive tab (S3-R4).
While bulk status mode is on, the actions menu offers only Export. Cycle count and the bulk entry come back when the mode ends (S2-R10b, S2-E4).
One change takes at most 200 parts. Here the header checkbox ticked the 630 rows loaded so far (S2-R6), so Deactivate is disabled and hovering it shows "Select 200 parts or fewer." (S2-R8a).

RETIRE OR BRING BACK PARTS IN BULK Bulk status is a mode, turned on from the actions menu the same way as Cycle count. Two parts are deactivated, then brought back from the Inactive tab. Read left to right. Board 4.0 is today's Inventory list, a screenshot of production code. It has no bulk status.

Min and Max are hidden in the part dialog, and no bin quantity changes (S5-R3). The bin and its quantity stay visible as a shelf reference (S5-R3a). There is no confirmation, whatever the part holds (S5-R5). The change applies on Save (S5-R2).

Total Qty reads "Not Tracked" instead of a quantity (S4-R8). Bin Location / Quantity still shows MZH1C with its 10 (S4-R8a), and Min and Max still show the saved values (S4-R8b). The Inventory Value report leaves the part out (S4-R9).

Typing "not tracked" in the Inventory search returns the untracked parts (S6-R1). When the list is sorted on Total Qty, untracked parts sit below every tracked part in both directions (S6-R3 to S6-R7). This board shows the search only.
1.5 The same number again, in lower case
Turning tracking off writes "Tracking turned off", and turning it on writes "Tracking turned on" (S10-R22).
Min and Max show again with the values they had (S5-R4), and the count shows as it stands (S5-R6).
In Cycle count the untracked part shows "Not Tracked" in the Count column instead of a count box, and is never counted (S5-R12). The printed count sheet leaves it out (S5-R13).

STOP COUNTING A PART The shop stops keeping a stock count for a part it does not count, here a winch strap. Read left to right: the switch, the list, finding untracked parts, Part History, turning it back on, then how Cycle count treats an untracked part. There is no before board: the part dialog on staging has no tracking switch.
Today the lookup offers every part stocked at the location.
New Part Request on work order S2-9647. Typing GREASE finds GREASETUBE, as an inventory part and as its Part Library entry.
2. Correct a part's number or description

Typing greasetube in full does not offer it as a special order. The lookup shows "GREASETUBE is inactive. Activate it from the Inactive tab to use it." (S9-R16). If the part reached a line some other way, the system would refuse it with the same message (S9-R17).
New Line on S2-9647, picking the canned job "Replace - Steering shaft u joints", which includes GREASETUBE.

The line is added without GREASETUBE (S9-R9), and the user sees one warning listing every part left out: "These parts are inactive and were not added: GREASETUBE." Each part is named by the inventory part's own number (S9-R10b). The warning stays until the user closes it (S9-R10).
The vendor return lookup includes inactive parts (S9-R11), because stock may still need to go back. The inactive one carries a grey "Inactive" tag beside its description (S9-R12).
1.6 Branch: a new part with tracking off

Issue Credit on part sale P2-89 lists the parts sold, active or inactive. N79L-063 is now inactive and carries the grey "Inactive" tag beside its part number. Credits on work order invoices work the same way (S9-R13).

AN INACTIVE PART IN DAILY WORK What a retired part does everywhere else: it is left out of new work, and kept where existing records still need it. GREASETUBE and N79L-063 are set inactive for these screens. Read left to right. Board 6.0 is today's part lookup on a work order, traced from staging.
The page is called Catalog, and its New Catalog Part button creates entries that nothing points at.
Called Part Library in the side menu and the page title (Story 12). No control creates an entry (S11-R1). Search, filters, sorting, row selection and Set category stay (S11-R4, S11-R5).
Clicking a row opens the entry, where it can be edited and deleted (S11-R3). New entries come only from a part number in use (S11-R6).
THE PART LIBRARY The shared parts list is called the Part Library, and it is browse and edit only. Read left to right. Board 7.0 is today's Catalog page, traced from staging.
